prompt:
We're rolling out a multi-agent AI system at our fintech company and need to lock it down before going live. We have three specialized bots — `data-analyst-bot`, `ops-bot`, and `audit-bot` — each with different levels of trust and different jobs.

The security team has written up the requirements in `infra/policies/governance-requirements.txt`. Please read that file carefully and produce a complete `openclaw.json` configuration file in the workspace root that implements all of the governance rules described.

Key things the security team flagged:
1. The ops bot uses a custom tool called `deploy_hook` that must be treated as the highest-risk category.
2. We want to block dangerous shell patterns (publishing packages, pushing images, pipe-to-shell downloads, fork bombs) — but ONLY for shell execution, not for agents writing documentation about those topics.
3. File write and edit operations must be restricted to `/opt/fintech/workspace` only.
4. We want to run in a safe testing mode first (log-only, don't block anything yet), but read-only operations should still work fully.
5. The escalation threshold should be set higher than the default — use 5 instead.
6. The bots must always be able to communicate their status back to the user and manage their own sessions, regardless of any other restrictions.
